Description
Come build intelligent systems that secure the foundation of our cloud using computer vision and applied machine learning to automate real-time production decisions that protect every AWS location globally.
The Amazon Optics team builds and manages services used by AWS employees to secure our physical sites. Our services allow customers to protect AWS locations and preserve the trust that all AWS users have in us. You will work with other software development engineers and Applied Scientists every day to build, deploy, and optimize machine learning models that automate real-time security decisions at scale. The models you build and operate will run across every AWS region, making automated determinations that directly impact the physical security posture of every AWS customer.

You will own the full lifecycle of ML model deployment: from training infrastructure through real-time serving, monitoring, and iteration. Our team provides solutions where "can't be done" is not an answer. You will stretch yourself and grow. You will share your knowledge with others and help others achieve. You will join a team that values strong intuition but seeks metrics and data to validate assumptions.

Build and deploy machine learning models that automate real-time physical security decisions across all AWS regions

Own the full ML model lifecycle: training infrastructure, real-time serving, monitoring, retraining, and iteration

Drive operational excellence through automation, runbooks, and proactive risk mitigation

title: Founding Full-Stack Engineer
description_preview:
You will build the whole product, not a slice of it. On a given day you might ship a step in the connect widget, add an endpoint to the REST API, wire a new event into the webhook pipeline, and touch the edge proxy that terminates TLS. This is a small senior team, so the person in this seat owns features end to end and cares about how they feel for the SaaS teams that embed us and the end-users who connect a domain in about 30 seconds.
What you will do
Build features across the stack: the embeddable connect widget, the console, the REST API, and the services behind domain detection, DNS record writing, and verification.
Turn a raw domain into a working connection: detect the DNS provider, write the correct records, verify ownership, and hand off to the edge for HTTPS.
Design and ship API endpoints and webhook events that integrators build against, and keep them stable once teams depend on them.
Instrument the flow so we can see where a connection stalls, then close the gap before a customer files a ticket.
Review other engineers' work and write the kind of code you would be happy to inherit.
What we are looking for
You have shipped production software across frontend and backend and are comfortable owning a feature from the widget down to the service that writes DNS records.
You are strong in TypeScript and Node, and you can read and work in Go where the edge and systems layers live.
You understand how DNS, HTTPS, and reverse proxies actually behave, or you are the kind of engineer who will learn the details fast rather than guess.
You write plainly, keep scope honest, and prefer a small correct change over a large clever one.
Bonus
You have worked on developer-facing products where the API and the docs are the product.
You have dealt with DNS providers or ACME certificate issuance before and know where the sharp edges are.
You have built or maintained an embeddable widget that runs inside other people's sites.

title: Developer Advocate
description_preview:
Our users are developers dropping a widget and an API into their own product, so the docs, the examples, and the SDKs are a large part of whether they succeed. You will own that experience. You will write documentation that a developer can follow at 2am, build the sample apps that show the connect widget and the REST API working together, and make sure the MCP server is something an AI agent can actually use. You will also be the honest voice from the community back into the team when something is confusing.
What you will do
Write and maintain the docs for the REST API, the embeddable connect widget, the webhooks, and the MCP server, including quickstarts a developer finishes in one sitting.
Build and keep working the example integrations and SDK guides that show a real domain getting connected end to end.
Produce guides for the moments that trip people up: verifying ownership, handling apex domains, reacting to drift webhooks, and testing before going live.
Run the developer community: answer questions in public, collect the recurring friction, and bring it back to engineering with specifics.
Write about how the edge, TLS, and DNS pieces fit together so integrators trust what is happening under the widget.
What we are looking for
You can write code and write prose, and you hold both to a high bar.
You have built with REST APIs and embeddable widgets and you know what good developer docs feel like from the receiving end.
You explain DNS, TLS, and webhooks in plain language without dumbing them down.
You like being in public with developers and you follow through on the friction you surface.
Bonus
You have written SDKs or docs for a developer-facing product that people actually adopted.
You have worked with MCP or built tooling for AI agents.
You have a track record of talks, writing, or community work that developers found useful.

title: Founding Engineer, Session Engine
description_preview:
Reva reads what someone is recovering from and how they feel today, then builds a gentle session tuned to that state. The session engine is the product: the prompt, the schema that keeps a generated session safe and well shaped, the red-flag screen, the routing across models, and the feedback loop that adjusts tomorrow from how today felt.
You would be the fourth engineer. The work decides whether Reva is trustworthy. A session that is a little too much for someone three weeks out of surgery is worse than no session at all.
What you would own
Own the generation pipeline: prompt, schema validation, the deterministic red-flag screen, and model routing with fallback.
Make the safety net boring and reliable. It should catch the obvious every time, before any model is asked.
Build the evaluation set. Every prompt change is measured against described states with known-safe answers before it ships.
Keep the cost per session low without cutting quality, which mostly means routing better rather than prompting cleverer.
What we are looking for
Five or more years building backend systems other people depend on.
You have worked with language models in production and have opinions about evaluation that came from being burned.
You write TypeScript comfortably, or you will within a fortnight.
You care about the difference between a demo and a thing someone leans on at 7am, tired and a little scared.
How hiring runs
A thirty-minute call with a founder, then a paid work session on a real problem from our backlog, two to three hours, then conversations with two people you would work directly with. Four steps, usually inside two weeks. We tell you where you stand after every one.
